    46	class GroupedGemmWgradSm100(APIBase):
    47	    """Stable public facade that selects the WGrad backend during support checking."""
    48	
    49	    # BF16 implementation
    50	    @overload
    51	    def __init__(
    52	        self,
    53	        sample_a: torch.Tensor,
    54	        sample_b: torch.Tensor,
    55	        sample_sfa: None,
    56	        sample_sfb: None,
    57	        sample_offsets: torch.Tensor,
    58	        *args: Any,
    59	        **kwargs: Any,
    60	    ) -> None: ...
    61	
    62	    # Block-scaled implementation
    63	    @overload
    64	    def __init__(
    65	        self,
    66	        sample_a: torch.Tensor,
    67	        sample_b: torch.Tensor,
    68	        sample_sfa: torch.Tensor,
    69	        sample_sfb: torch.Tensor,
    70	        sample_offsets: torch.Tensor,
    71	        *args: Any,
    72	        **kwargs: Any,
    73	    ) -> None: ...
    74	
    75	    def __init__(
    76	        self,
    77	        sample_a: torch.Tensor,
    78	        sample_b: torch.Tensor,
    79	        sample_sfa: Optional[torch.Tensor],
    80	        sample_sfb: Optional[torch.Tensor],
    81	        sample_offsets: torch.Tensor,
    82	        sample_wgrad: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    83	        sample_wgrad_expert: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    84	        num_experts: Optional[int] = None,
    85	        wgrad_shape: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None,
    86	        wgrad_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
    87	        sample_global_scale_a: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    88	        sample_global_scale_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    89	        acc_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
    90	        mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int] = (256, 256),
    91	        cluster_shape_mn: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None,
    92	        sf_vec_size: int = 16,
    93	        accumulate_on_output: bool = False,
    94	        input_order: WGradInputOrder | str = WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D,
    95	    ) -> None:
    96	        super().__init__()
    97	        self._pending_init_kwargs = dict(locals())
    98	        self._pending_init_kwargs.pop("self")
    99	        self._pending_init_kwargs.pop("__class__", None)
   100	        self._implementation = None
   101	
   102	    def check_support(self) -> bool:
   103	        if self._implementation is None:
   104	            kwargs = self._pending_init_kwargs
   105	            backend = select_grouped_gemm_backend(
   106	                operation="grouped_gemm_wgrad_sm100",
   107	                a_dtype=kwargs["sample_a"].dtype,
   108	                b_dtype=kwargs["sample_b"].dtype,
   109	                scale_controls=(
   110	                    ("sample_sfa", kwargs["sample_sfa"]),
   111	                    ("sample_sfb", kwargs["sample_sfb"]),
   112	                    ("sample_global_scale_a", kwargs["sample_global_scale_a"]),
   113	                    ("sample_global_scale_b", kwargs["sample_global_scale_b"]),
   114	                    ("sf_vec_size", kwargs["sf_vec_size"] if kwargs["sf_vec_size"] != 16 else None),
   115	                ),
   116	                block_scaled_dtype_pairs=_BLOCK_SCALED_DTYPE_PAIRS,
   117	            )
   118	            self.backend = backend
   119	            if backend is GroupedGemmBackend.BF16:
   120	                self._implementation = GroupedGemmWgradBf16API(**kwargs)
   121	            else:
   122	                self._implementation = GroupedGemmWgradBlockScaledAPI(**kwargs)
   123	            self._kernel = self._implementation._kernel
   124	            self.weight_mode = self._implementation.weight_mode
   125	        supported = self._implementation.check_support()
   126	        self._is_supported = self._implementation._is_supported
   127	        if supported:
   128	            self._pending_init_kwargs = None
   129	        return supported
   130	
   131	    def compile(self) -> None:
   132	        if self._implementation is None:
   133	            self.check_support()
   134	        if self._is_supported:
   135	            self._implementation._is_supported = True
   136	        self._implementation.compile()
   137	        self._is_supported = self._implementation._is_supported
   138	        self._compiled_kernel = self._implementation._compiled_kernel
   139	
   140	    # BF16 implementation
   141	    @overload
   142	    def execute(
   143	        self,
   144	        a_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   145	        b_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   146	        sfa_tensor: None,
   147	        sfb_tensor: None,
   148	        offsets_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   149	        wgrad_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   150	        wgrad_ptrs: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   151	        *,
   152	        global_scale_a: None = None,
   153	        global_scale_b: None = None,
   154	    ) -> None: ...
   155	
   156	    # Block-scaled implementation
   157	    @overload
   158	    def execute(
   159	        self,
   160	        a_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   161	        b_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   162	        sfa_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   163	        sfb_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   164	        offsets_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   165	        wgrad_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   166	        wgrad_ptrs: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   167	        *,
   168	        global_scale_a: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   169	        global_scale_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   170	    ) -> None: ...
   171	
   172	    def execute(
   173	        self,
   174	        a_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   175	        b_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   176	        sfa_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   177	        sfb_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   178	        offsets_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   179	        wgrad_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   180	        wgrad_ptrs: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   181	        global_scale_a: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   182	        global_scale_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   183	        current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None,
   184	    ) -> None:
   185	        if self._implementation is None:
   186	            raise RuntimeError("Kernel not compiled; call compile() first")
   187	        self._implementation.execute(
   188	            a_tensor=a_tensor,
   189	            b_tensor=b_tensor,
   190	            sfa_tensor=sfa_tensor,
   191	            sfb_tensor=sfb_tensor,
   192	            offsets_tensor=offsets_tensor,
   193	            wgrad_tensor=wgrad_tensor,
   194	            wgrad_ptrs=wgrad_ptrs,
   195	            global_scale_a=global_scale_a,
   196	            global_scale_b=global_scale_b,
   197	            current_stream=current_stream,
   198	        )
   199	
   200	
   201	def _wgrad_tensor_signature(tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor], *, dynamic_dims: tuple[int, ...] = (), exact_stride: bool):
   202	    if tensor is None:
   203	        return None
   204	    shape = tuple(None if index in dynamic_dims else int(value) for index, value in enumerate(tensor.shape))
   205	    stride = tuple(int(value) for value in tensor.stride())
   206	    layout = stride if exact_stride else tuple(index for index, _ in sorted(enumerate(stride), key=lambda item: (item[1], tensor.shape[item[0]])))
   207	    return (shape, layout, tensor.dtype, tensor.device)
   208	
   209	
   210	def grouped_gemm_wgrad_wrapper_sm100(
   211	    a_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   212	    b_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   213	    sfa_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   214	    sfb_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   215	    offsets_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   216	    output_mode: str = "dense",
   217	    wgrad_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   218	    wgrad_ptrs: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   219	    global_scale_a: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   220	    global_scale_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   221	    acc_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
   222	    wgrad_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
   223	    mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int] = (256, 256),
   224	    cluster_shape_mn: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None,
   225	    sf_vec_size: int = 16,
   226	    accumulate_on_output: bool = False,
   227	    input_order: WGradInputOrder | str = WGradInputOrder.Tensor2D,
   228	    current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None,
   229	) -> TupleDict:
   230	    """Compile and execute grouped GEMM wgrad through the selected backend API."""
   231	    if output_mode not in ("dense", "discrete"):
   232	        raise ValueError(f'output_mode must be "dense" or "discrete", got {output_mode}')
   233	    if a_tensor.ndim != 2 or b_tensor.ndim != 2:
   234	        raise ValueError("a_tensor and b_tensor must both be rank-2")
   235	    hidden, tokens_sum = a_tensor.shape
   236	    tokens_b, intermediate = b_tensor.shape
   237	    if tokens_sum != tokens_b:
   238	        raise ValueError(f"a_tensor and b_tensor token dimensions must match, got {tokens_sum} and {tokens_b}")
   239	    if offsets_tensor.ndim != 1:
   240	        raise ValueError(f"offsets_tensor must be rank-1, got shape {tuple(offsets_tensor.shape)}")
   241	    input_order = WGradInputOrder(input_order)
   242	    expert_cnt = offsets_tensor.numel()
   243	    if output_mode == "dense" and wgrad_ptrs is not None:
   244	        raise ValueError("dense output_mode forbids wgrad_ptrs")
   245	    if wgrad_ptrs is not None:
   246	        _require_pointer_tensor(wgrad_ptrs, "wgrad_ptrs", expert_cnt)
   247	    backend = select_grouped_gemm_backend(
   248	        operation="grouped_gemm_wgrad_sm100",
   249	        a_dtype=a_tensor.dtype,
   250	        b_dtype=b_tensor.dtype,
   251	        scale_controls=(
   252	            ("sfa_tensor", sfa_tensor),
   253	            ("sfb_tensor", sfb_tensor),
   254	            ("global_scale_a", global_scale_a),
   255	            ("global_scale_b", global_scale_b),
   256	            ("sf_vec_size", sf_vec_size if sf_vec_size != 16 else None),
   257	        ),
   258	        block_scaled_dtype_pairs=_BLOCK_SCALED_DTYPE_PAIRS,
   259	    )
   260	    if wgrad_tensor is None and wgrad_ptrs is None:
   440	        if desc.dtype != self.wgrad_dtype:
   441	            raise ValueError(f"wgrad_tensor dtype mismatch: expected {self.wgrad_dtype}, got {desc.dtype}")
   442	        if desc.device != self.a_desc.device:
   443	            raise ValueError(f"wgrad_tensor device mismatch: expected {self.a_desc.device}, got {desc.device}")
   444	
   445	    def execute(
   446	        self,
   447	        a_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   448	        b_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   449	        sfa_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor],
   450	        sfb_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor],
   451	        offsets_tensor: torch.Tensor,
   452	        wgrad_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   453	        wgrad_ptrs: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   454	        global_scale_a: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   455	        global_scale_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
   456	        current_stream: Optional[cuda.CUstream] = None,
   457	    ) -> None:
   458	        current_stream = self._get_default_stream(current_stream)
   459	        if self._compiled_kernel is None:
   460	            raise RuntimeError("Kernel not compiled; call compile() first")
   461	        forbidden = (
   462	            ("sfa_tensor", sfa_tensor),
   463	            ("sfb_tensor", sfb_tensor),
   464	            ("global_scale_a", global_scale_a),
   465	            ("global_scale_b", global_scale_b),
   466	        )
   467	        for name, value in forbidden:
   468	            if value is not None:
   469	                raise ValueError(f"BF16 forbids scale control {name}")
   470	        a_desc = self._validate_live_input(a_tensor, self.a_desc, "a_tensor", token_axis=1)
   471	        b_desc = self._validate_live_input(b_tensor, self.b_desc, "b_tensor", token_axis=0)
   472	        tokens_sum = a_desc.shape[1]
   473	        if b_desc.shape[0] != tokens_sum:
   474	            raise ValueError("a_tensor and b_tensor token dimensions must match")
   475	        offsets_desc = self._make_tensor_desc(offsets_tensor, name="offsets_tensor")
   476	        if offsets_desc.shape != (self.expert_cnt,) or offsets_desc.stride != (1,) or offsets_desc.dtype != torch.int32:
   477	            raise ValueError("offsets_tensor must be a contiguous rank-1 int32 tensor with one entry per expert")
   478	        if offsets_desc.device != self.a_desc.device:
   479	            raise ValueError(f"offsets_tensor device mismatch: expected {self.a_desc.device}, got {offsets_desc.device}")
   480	        self._validate_offsets_once(offsets_tensor, tokens_sum=tokens_sum)
   481	        self._validate_data_alignment(a_tensor, "a_tensor")
   482	        self._validate_data_alignment(b_tensor, "b_tensor")
   483	        self._validate_data_alignment(offsets_tensor, "offsets_tensor", 4)
   484	
   485	        if self.weight_mode == MoEWeightMode.DENSE:
   486	            if wgrad_tensor is None or wgrad_ptrs is not None:
   487	                raise ValueError("Dense execution requires wgrad_tensor and forbids wgrad_ptrs")
   488	            self._validate_live_output(wgrad_tensor)
   489	            self._validate_data_alignment(wgrad_tensor, "wgrad_tensor")
   490	            output = wgrad_tensor
   491	        else:
   492	            if wgrad_tensor is not None:
   493	                self._validate_live_output(wgrad_tensor)
   494	                self._validate_data_alignment(wgrad_tensor, "wgrad_tensor")
   495	            generated_wgrad_ptrs = wgrad_ptrs is None
   496	            if wgrad_ptrs is None:
   497	                if wgrad_tensor is None:
   498	                    raise ValueError("Discrete execution requires wgrad_tensor or wgrad_ptrs")
   499	                stride_bytes = wgrad_tensor.stride(0) * wgrad_tensor.element_size()
   500	                with _torch_stream_context(current_stream, wgrad_tensor.device):
   501	                    wgrad_ptrs = torch.tensor(
   502	                        [wgrad_tensor.data_ptr() + index * stride_bytes for index in range(self.expert_cnt)],
   503	                        dtype=torch.int64,
   504	                        device=wgrad_tensor.device,
   505	                    )
   506	            _require_pointer_tensor(wgrad_ptrs, "wgrad_ptrs", self.expert_cnt)
   507	            if wgrad_ptrs.device != self.a_desc.device:
   508	                raise ValueError(f"wgrad_ptrs must be on {self.a_desc.device}, got {wgrad_ptrs.device}")
   509	            self._validate_pointer_array_alignment(wgrad_ptrs)
   510	            if not generated_wgrad_ptrs:
   511	                self._validate_pointer_values_once(wgrad_ptrs)
   512	            self._record_pointer_stream(wgrad_ptrs, current_stream)
   513	            output = wgrad_ptrs
   514	        self._compiled_kernel(a_tensor, b_tensor, output, offsets_tensor, current_stream)

## Verdict: incorrect

The current ragged hero path computes silently wrong expert-weight gradients. Both `dw13`—therefore `w_gate` and `w_up`—and `dw2`/`w_down` are passed to an unsupported cuDNN Frontend 1.27.0 grouped-Wgrad kernel configuration.

Confidence is high for the dispatch and contract violation. Confidence in the exact error distribution is moderate because no SM100 GPU was available here; historical GB200 measurements were not rerun.

### Actual production dispatch

I audited HEAD `85caf4210b32404839aab07c85bd875e7bd0dad1` plus the dirty working tree. The current branch’s hero model specifies d6144, expert width/intermediate width 3072, 384 experts, top-8, 48 layers, capacity factor 1.15, and `ragged_all_to_all` in [heuristic.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py:85). The recipe supplies EP64 and BF16 compute in [hero_recipe.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_recipe.py:33) and [hero_recipe.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_recipe.py:41); parameters are cast to compute dtype before `jax.value_and_grad` in [train.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py:873).

The resulting path is:

1. `ActivationFunctionEnum.silu` resolves to the exact `jax.nn.silu` function object in [activation.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/utils/activation.py:63).

That confirms runtime selection rather than merely inferring from available kernels.

### Contract audit

JAX ragged all-to-all: no violation found. JAX 0.11.1 requires equal-length, nonempty integer metadata vectors, length divisible by the mapped-axis size, and matching transposed send/receive sizes in [parallel.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/jax/_src/lax/parallel.py:631). Marin constructs 384 entries—EP64 × six local experts—and dispatch/return as exact mirrors in [ep_common.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_common.py:147). Its custom VJP performs the same swapped sizes, exchanged offsets, reverse collective, and overwritten-output masking as JAX’s own transpose rule; compare [ep_ragged_all_to_all.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py:344) with [parallel.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/jax/_src/lax/parallel.py:1692).

QuACK forward and activation gradients: no visible contract violation found. The pinned 0.6.1 wrapper declares BF16 support and 8-element vector alignment in [quack_moe_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/quack_moe_cute.py:77). Hero dimensions 3072 and 6144 meet the layout constraints; cumulative group offsets are int32 and have length four for each three-expert call. The forward/down/dgrad logical weight layouts match the wrapper’s `b_major="n"` and `"k"` mappings. This integration directly uses QuACK kernel classes rather than a separately documented stable JAX facade, which remains an API-stability risk, but I found no hero-shape contract mismatch.

Sonic combine: no violation found. On GPU the fused gather/sum uses FP32 accumulation and its backward writes one result per unique dispatch position in [sonic.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic.py:289). Its hidden-width limit covers the hero’s latent width 3072.

cuDNN Wgrad: definite violation. Marin pins cuDNN Frontend 1.27.0 in [pyproject.toml](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/pyproject.toml:93) and [uv.lock](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/uv.lock:5764). That exact package’s shipped API requires:

- Every expert token count to be divisible by 256.
- The final cumulative offset to equal the input token dimension.
- BF16 inputs, int32 offsets, FP32 accumulation, compatible contiguous layouts and pointer alignment.
- SM100 or newer.
- A successful internal `can_implement` call.

See the installed package’s [_bf16_api.py](/home/marin/.cache/uv/archive-v0/XG3ddyF2LTqrNQ-M/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/_bf16_api.py:135) and [NVIDIA’s 1.27 documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/v1.27.0/fe-oss-apis/gemm_fusions/grouped_gemm_wgrad.html). The internal kernel itself declares `FIX_PAD_SIZE = 256` and rejects other group lengths in [moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad.py](/home/marin/.cache/uv/archive-v0/XG3ddyF2LTqrNQ-M/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad.py:75).

Marin instead:

- Imports the private internal kernel class directly in [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:36).
- Pads groups only to eight rows at [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:74).
- Calls the raw kernel without the public `check_support` or internal `can_implement` check at [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:50).

A CPU probe of the actual padding helper showed:

```text
backend= cpu
input_rows= 301466 padded_rows= 301487
active_sizes= [100489, 100488, 100489]
padded_sizes= [100496, 100488, 100496]
padded_sizes_mod_256= [144, 136, 144]
last_offset= 301480
```

This probe does not test the GPU kernel. It proves that the wrapper’s metadata fails the documented 256-row requirement. At the fixed hero shape, the padded physical row count is `301466 + 7×3 = 301487`, while the final offset is always divisible by eight, so the public final-offset equality can never hold either.

The dirty working-tree changes add an optional prealigned receiver layout, but the hero leaves `ragged_receiver_alignment=None`; `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` remains eight. They do not fix the contract failure.

### History and numerical evidence

Repository and GitHub history corroborate the defect:

$ git log --all --follow -- .../cudnn_wgrad_cute.py

[Issue #8339](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339) reports direct GB200 errors of 0.17–0.55 relative to the gradient peak at production-like dimensions, versus a BF16 floor near 0.003. Its [later contract correction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339#issuecomment-5318708904) reports relative error 0.269 with eight-row alignment, 0.217 with 32, and zero with 64—but correctly notes that even 64 remains outside the supported 256-row contract.

The issue was closed without a fix reaching this branch. Commit `f2c9f702f3` changed eight to 64 only on a separate lineage and is not an ancestor of HEAD. [PR #8549](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8549) later merged the eight-row wrapper as `dc584e765d...`. Its reported green four-GPU test is not dispositive: the harness gates gradients on a 5% worst-slice median while ignoring the recorded maximum in [ragged_ep.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py:84) and [ragged_ep.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py:406). The accelerator test is explicitly unscheduled in [test_ragged_ep_check.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/tests/cluster/grug/test_ragged_ep_check.py:4).

The two passes covered the portable SwiGLU backward formula. The end-to-end ragged value/gradient tests skipped. No JAX ragged collective, QuACK kernel, cuDNN Wgrad kernel, or SM100 execution occurred locally.

### Blast radius

For every affected backward step:

- All 48 routed-MoE layers are affected.
- Every EP rank processes two chunks with three local experts each.
- `dw13` has per-call shape `[3, 3072, 6144]`, contaminating both `w_gate` and `w_up`.
- `dw2` has per-call shape `[3, 3072, 3072]`, contaminating `w_down`.
- That is two unsupported Wgrad calls × two chunks × 48 layers = 192 unsupported calls per rank per training step.
- Forward outputs and same-step expert-input/router/combine gradients are not directly produced by the faulty Wgrad call. Subsequent steps are nevertheless contaminated after the optimizer applies the corrupted expert-weight updates.

The historical 17–55% peak-relative errors demonstrate potentially large entrywise corruption, but they are not an exact measurement of the current latent-hero tensor shapes. The current error distribution, affected-entry fraction, and loss impact are therefore undetermined.

One important boundary: the original long-running 18T hero launched at commit `12d8b6f...` used `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, not this ragged/cuDNN path, as documented in [issue #8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5335872267). Current ragged hero launches, checkpoint-restored diagnostics, and future training from the branch default are in the blast radius; the immutable original pooled-wave launch is not.

### Confidence and limitations

- High confidence that current SM100+SiLU ragged hero dispatches to this Wgrad wrapper.
- High confidence that the supplied inputs violate both the documented facade and the raw kernel’s own 256-row `can_implement` requirement.
- High confidence that both expert weight-gradient tensors are affected.
- Moderate confidence in the historical magnitude’s transfer to the exact current shapes.
- No local GPU evidence. CPU results were used only for portable algebra and metadata construction.

| SwiGLU derivative | JAX arithmetic in `_swiglu_gate_up_backward` |
| `dw2` | cuDNN `MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel` |
| `dw13` | cuDNN `MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel` |

The two Wgrad calls are explicit at [sonic_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic_cute.py:117). A recorded hero-shape xprof also identifies `pad_grouped_rows` as the immediate predecessor of the cuDNN dW13 call, with the exact 301,487-row padded operand, in [LOGBOOK.md](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/autoresearch/loop-260828-8753mfu/LOGBOOK.md:1023). That confirms runtime selection rather than merely inferring from available kernels.

### Contract audit

JAX ragged all-to-all: no violation found. JAX 0.11.1 requires equal-length, nonempty integer metadata vectors, length divisible by the mapped-axis size, and matching transposed send/receive sizes in [parallel.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/jax/_src/lax/parallel.py:631). Marin constructs 384 entries—EP64 × six local experts—and dispatch/return as exact mirrors in [ep_common.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_common.py:147). Its custom VJP performs the same swapped sizes, exchanged offsets, reverse collective, and overwritten-output masking as JAX’s own transpose rule; compare [ep_ragged_all_to_all.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py:344) with [parallel.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/jax/_src/lax/parallel.py:1692).

QuACK forward and activation gradients: no visible contract violation found. The pinned 0.6.1 wrapper declares BF16 support and 8-element vector alignment in [quack_moe_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/quack_moe_cute.py:77). Hero dimensions 3072 and 6144 meet the layout constraints; cumulative group offsets are int32 and have length four for each three-expert call. The forward/down/dgrad logical weight layouts match the wrapper’s `b_major="n"` and `"k"` mappings. This integration directly uses QuACK kernel classes rather than a separately documented stable JAX facade, which remains an API-stability risk, but I found no hero-shape contract mismatch.

Sonic combine: no violation found. On GPU the fused gather/sum uses FP32 accumulation and its backward writes one result per unique dispatch position in [sonic.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic.py:289). Its hidden-width limit covers the hero’s latent width 3072.

cuDNN Wgrad: definite violation. Marin pins cuDNN Frontend 1.27.0 in [pyproject.toml](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/pyproject.toml:93) and [uv.lock](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/uv.lock:5764). That exact package’s shipped API requires:

- Every expert token count to be divisible by 256.
- The final cumulative offset to equal the input token dimension.
- BF16 inputs, int32 offsets, FP32 accumulation, compatible contiguous layouts and pointer alignment.
- SM100 or newer.
- A successful internal `can_implement` call.

See the installed package’s [_bf16_api.py](/home/marin/.cache/uv/archive-v0/XG3ddyF2LTqrNQ-M/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/_bf16_api.py:135) and [NVIDIA’s 1.27 documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/v1.27.0/fe-oss-apis/gemm_fusions/grouped_gemm_wgrad.html). The internal kernel itself declares `FIX_PAD_SIZE = 256` and rejects other group lengths in [moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad.py](/home/marin/.cache/uv/archive-v0/XG3ddyF2LTqrNQ-M/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad.py:75).

Marin instead:

- Imports the private internal kernel class directly in [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:36).
- Pads groups only to eight rows at [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:74).
- Calls the raw kernel without the public `check_support` or internal `can_implement` check at [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:50).

A CPU probe of the actual padding helper showed:

```text
backend= cpu
input_rows= 301466 padded_rows= 301487
active_sizes= [100489, 100488, 100489]
padded_sizes= [100496, 100488, 100496]
padded_sizes_mod_256= [144, 136, 144]
last_offset= 301480
```

This probe does not test the GPU kernel. It proves that the wrapper’s metadata fails the documented 256-row requirement. At the fixed hero shape, the padded physical row count is `301466 + 7×3 = 301487`, while the final offset is always divisible by eight, so the public final-offset equality can never hold either.

The dirty working-tree changes add an optional prealigned receiver layout, but the hero leaves `ragged_receiver_alignment=None`; `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` remains eight. They do not fix the contract failure.

### History and numerical evidence

Repository and GitHub history corroborate the defect:

```text
$ git log --all --follow -- .../cudnn_wgrad_cute.py
dc584e765d 2026-08-27 [grug] Rework ... (#8549)
583fa2830d 2026-08-20 [grug] Compute ... on cuDNN grouped kernels
f2c9f702f3 2026-08-16 ... needs 64-aligned group offsets

$ git merge-base --is-ancestor f2c9f702f3 HEAD
exit 1
```

[Issue #8339](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339) reports direct GB200 errors of 0.17–0.55 relative to the gradient peak at production-like dimensions, versus a BF16 floor near 0.003. Its [later contract correction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8339#issuecomment-5318708904) reports relative error 0.269 with eight-row alignment, 0.217 with 32, and zero with 64—but correctly notes that even 64 remains outside the supported 256-row contract.

The issue was closed without a fix reaching this branch. Commit `f2c9f702f3` changed eight to 64 only on a separate lineage and is not an ancestor of HEAD. [PR #8549](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8549) later merged the eight-row wrapper as `dc584e765d...`. Its reported green four-GPU test is not dispositive: the harness gates gradients on a 5% worst-slice median while ignoring the recorded maximum in [ragged_ep.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py:84) and [ragged_ep.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py:406). The accelerator test is explicitly unscheduled in [test_ragged_ep_check.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/tests/cluster/grug/test_ragged_ep_check.py:4).

Local CPU tests:

```text

SKIPPED [2] ... requires an even number of >=2 devices
2 passed, 2 skipped
```

The two passes covered the portable SwiGLU backward formula. The end-to-end ragged value/gradient tests skipped. No JAX ragged collective, QuACK kernel, cuDNN Wgrad kernel, or SM100 execution occurred locally.

### Blast radius

For every affected backward step:

- All 48 routed-MoE layers are affected.
- Every EP rank processes two chunks with three local experts each.
- `dw13` has per-call shape `[3, 3072, 6144]`, contaminating both `w_gate` and `w_up`.
- `dw2` has per-call shape `[3, 3072, 3072]`, contaminating `w_down`.
- That is two unsupported Wgrad calls × two chunks × 48 layers = 192 unsupported calls per rank per training step.
- Forward outputs and same-step expert-input/router/combine gradients are not directly produced by the faulty Wgrad call. Subsequent steps are nevertheless contaminated after the optimizer applies the corrupted expert-weight updates.

The historical 17–55% peak-relative errors demonstrate potentially large entrywise corruption, but they are not an exact measurement of the current latent-hero tensor shapes. The current error distribution, affected-entry fraction, and loss impact are therefore undetermined.

One important boundary: the original long-running 18T hero launched at commit `12d8b6f...` used `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, not this ragged/cuDNN path, as documented in [issue #8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5335872267). Current ragged hero launches, checkpoint-restored diagnostics, and future training from the branch default are in the blast radius; the immutable original pooled-wave launch is not.

### Confidence and limitations

- High confidence that current SM100+SiLU ragged hero dispatches to this Wgrad wrapper.
- High confidence that the supplied inputs violate both the documented facade and the raw kernel’s own 256-row `can_implement` requirement.
- High confidence that both expert weight-gradient tensors are affected.
- Moderate confidence in the historical magnitude’s transfer to the exact current shapes.
- No local GPU evidence. CPU results were used only for portable algebra and metadata construction.

15276:{"body":"Issue is to describe the Hero Run scaling ladder, config, and track its performance.\n\nTracking: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng\n\nDetails on the full model spec is in the comment below.\n\n### Why run a scaling ladder?\n\n1. This lets us project the model performance and compare it to the scaling projections of our prior recipes. If our projection looks meaningfully worse, then we know we need to go back to the drawing board on some aspect of the model or data. This step can catch a lot of bugs!\n2. We can look at how training dynamics change as we scale, in particular the gradient norms and token dropping. In our last run, the scaling ladder caught gradient norm growth to over 4 as we scaled out token horizon, which caused us to find a fix with logit z loss. Later ablations showed that without this fix, runs under certain conditions like high batch size would completely blow up mid-run.\n3. We can project our evals across the entire trajectory of the run. This means that across the entire ~100 day run, we know exactly how we are doing compared to the projection. If at any point we fail to match the projection, it can prompt early investigation into training dynamics.\n4. If something strange start to happen in the Hero run, we can reference the smaller scales runs to see if its actually normal. For instance, in prior scaling ladders we saw the grad norm grow heavily up to 40% of the run, then decrease as the LR decays. When we saw this on the hero run, having the small scale reference gave us confidence we didn't need to intervene, as long as the gradient followed the same pattern (steady growth for 40% of run).\n5. It only costs 1% of total compute.\n### What is our EP hardware implementation?\nDescribed in detail here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html.\nWe are hand-rolling our own EP implementation, props to @ravwojdyla, since we have not found a more performant variant on JAX XLA on GPU. \n\n### What is our long context extension plan?\nOur last run was 8k seqlen pretrain, followed by 65k extension for 1T tokens, followed by 262k extension (to occur end of Aug). Prior to that run we have used 4k seqlen pretrain. For this run we are going back to 4k seqlen pretrain to start, to enable better expert balancing (twice as many sequences per batch). We wanted to minimize risk here because our EP token dropping implementation is more experimental. (our last run was dropless FSDP). Prior tests showed token dropping grow from ~7% to ~40% when extending from 4k to 65k seqlen. Our new pooled/wave EP drops about half as many tokens (3%) at 4k seqlen; however the token dropping is likely still excessively high at 65k seqlen.\n\nWe will spend 1-2 days to do an early cooldown at roughly 10-20 days into the run, to enable RL experiments, which will be our first full scale data point at how longer context influences dropping. A nice property of this test is that the cooldown will not contaminate or impact the main run, so we have some flexibility to collect data on how an extension approach impacts dropping. Our options will be:\n1. If we have landed a Jax Mixture of Kittens or dropless ragged all-to-all, then we can swap to that for the cooldown. Prior small scale tests showed the model was robust from swapping from small amounts of dropping (5%) to dropless mid-run.\n2. Otherwise, we can increase our capacity factor, and accept some amount of dropping.\n3. If we find that neither of these options are suitable, the next option would be to introduce sequence level balancing mid-run (though forcing the experts to re-specialize mid-run will likely be worse than accepting some amount of dropping). \n\nExtending context will involve updating qk_mult according to mscale=X⋅ln(new_seqlen/old_seqlen)+1, testing coefficients near 0.1 (can quickly eval a range during extension on 1 rack). If the data from the first cooldown looks smooth, will plan on 4k-\u003e8k at 50 pct into run, then 8k-\u003e65k at about 95 pct, then a targeted 262k phase near end, based on data we collect from taking the 67B-A2B from 65k to 262k.\n\nHave further derisked token dropping by staying at 2 shared experts, each at half width. 8 active experts are also at half width. Having 1/3 of our neurons come from shared expert will provide a stronger backbone in the event of high dropping. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.\n\n## 1. Model\n\n### Hyperparameters\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| hidden_dim | 6144 |\n| num_layers | 48 |\n| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |\n| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |\n| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |\n| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |\n| vocab_size | 128,256 |\n| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |\n| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |\n| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |\n| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |\n| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |\n| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |\n\n### Features\nAll structural (always on) unless noted.\n- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.\n- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.\n- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.\n- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).\n- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)\n- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.\n- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.\n- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).\n- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.\n- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).\n- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.\n- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).\n- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.\n- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.\n- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.\n- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.\n- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.\n\n## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)\n\nThree groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:\n- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.\n- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.\n- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.\n\n### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |\n| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |\n| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |\n| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |\n| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |\n| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |\n| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |\n| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |\n| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |\n\nThe MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.\n\n## 3. Training \u0026 topology\n- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.\n- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.\n- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).\n- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.\n- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).\n\n## 4. MFU / performance optimizations\n- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)\n- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.\n- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.\n- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.\n- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation=\"xla_fast_bwd\"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.\n- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.\n- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.\n- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.\n- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.\n- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:\n  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.\n  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.\n  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.\n- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.\n- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.\n- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.\n- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)\n- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.\n\n## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)\nRuns at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.\n\n| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |\n| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |\n| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |\n| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |\n| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |\n\n## 6. I have a question regarding the motivation behind LatentMoE. Since the training system uses GB200 NVL72 with high-bandwidth NVLink, I am curious why a latent representation is introduced before expert dispatch. Is LatentMoE mainly motivated by reducing communication overhead at larger scales (e.g., beyond a single NVLink domain), or does it also provide benefits beyond communication optimization, such as improving model capability? Thanks!\n\nOn its own, LatentMoE halves the comms cost. We found that putting a learnable RMSNorm on the latent projection improved model capability as well, so LatentMoE w/ norm performed better than no latent MoE. Without this learnable RMSNorm, we run into activation scaling issue and see 30 percent worse quality. We also found going from top 4 of 192 to top 8 of 384 (half sized) gave 15 percent quality gain. But it doubles comms cost. So one way to view latentMoE is it enables 4/192-\u003e8/384 without change to either comms or compute.","createdAt":"2026-08-25T06:53:00Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5406648997"},{"body":"Thanks for the detailed reply! We never ended up doing large scale ablation here, since I was more worried about token dropping dynamics. Also the way we are using jax scan makes it a awkward to have different behavior per layer. I am less optimistic about alternating dense/moe long term, because with mature mixture-of-kittens kernels the MFU hit of MoE is probably not that high anyways.\n2. Hmm I separately saw some early positive results from Inkling relative position embedding that gave lower loss. But our kernel was not quite fast enough to justify. And perhaps more importantly, the kernel was a bit buggy if I changed sliding window length. I think it should be good on global layers too, since its limited to just the most recent X (512 or 1024) positions. I am more bullish on relative position embedding + MLA. Since MLA has very janky approach to RoPE, which requires replicating 64 head dims across every head. Relative position embedding fixes this. Have to be a bit careful with ablations here because at very small scale RoPE on global looks much better than NoPE on global. (but this fades with scale)\n3. So initial AdamH on embed looked good. But later I did learning rate sweep, and if LR was 40% too high, was seeing grad spikes up to 20. I think what was happening (guessing) was rare tokens were having their norm driven to near zero, and then getting massive grad when they finally ended up in the batch. (we have rms_norm on embed that will apply high growth multiplier to small vocab embeds) Dont want any features in the model that require perfectly optimal hypers. So reverted it.\n\n\u003cimg width=\"874\" height=\"552\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/096aaa54-f17f-4e96-8a8e-a1a825f84270\" /\u003e","createdAt":"2026-08-27T01:23:04Z","url":"https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5433154702"},{"body":"Thanks, this is really helpful.\n\nMy motivation for alternating dense/MoE is less about the current MFU gap and more about separation of concerns: dense layers handle common computation, while MoE layers handle specialization. Keeping them as two clean execution patterns seems to leave more room for independent kernel, scheduling, and parallelism optimization, even if MoE kernels improve substantially.\n\nFor position encoding, my preference for learned relative PE on local layers + NoPE on global layers is mainly to avoid positional extrapolation entirely. With a fixed local window, the relative-position range never changes as context grows, while global attention stays purely content-addressed. 15284:2026-08-19T00:15:31Z	https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-5335872267	🤖 # Job Summary: Aug Hero Run — 535B-A23B MoE (d6144), 18T tokens\n\nFull-scale EP64 MoE pretrain: d6144, **535.3B total / 22.76B active** params, **18.0T tokens** (~**2.70e24** train FLOPs, fwd+bwd), on GB200 with our hand-rolled pooled-wave expert-parallel all-to-all. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.\n\n## 1. Model\n\n### Hyperparameters\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| hidden_dim | 6144 |\n| num_layers | 48 |\n| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |\n| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |\n| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |\n| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |\n| vocab_size | 128,256 |\n| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |\n| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |\n| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |\n| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |\n| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |\n| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |\n\n### Features\nAll structural (always on) unless noted.\n- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.\n- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.\n- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.\n- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).\n- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)\n- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.\n- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.\n- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).\n- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.\n- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).\n- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.\n- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).\n- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.\n- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.\n- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.\n- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.\n- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.\n\n## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)\n\nThree groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:\n- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.\n- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.\n- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.\n\n### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |\n| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |\n| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |\n| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |\n| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |\n| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |\n| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |\n| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |\n| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |\n\nThe MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.\n\n## 3. Training & topology\n- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.\n- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.\n- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).\n- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.\n- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).\n\n## 4. MFU / performance optimizations\n- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)\n- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.\n- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.\n- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.\n- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation="xla_fast_bwd"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.\n- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.\n- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.\n- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.\n- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.\n- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:\n  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.\n  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.\n  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.\n- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.\n- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.\n- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.\n- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)\n- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.\n\n## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)\nRuns at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.\n\n| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |\n| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |\n| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |\n| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |\n| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |\n\n## 6.
