19050:{"comments":[{"body":"🤖 # Job Summary: Aug Hero Run — 535B-A23B MoE (d6144), 18T tokens\n\nFull-scale EP64 MoE pretrain: d6144, **535.3B total / 22.76B active** params, **18.0T tokens** (~**2.70e24** train FLOPs, fwd+bwd), on GB200 with our hand-rolled pooled-wave expert-parallel all-to-all. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.\n\n## 1. Model\n\n### Hyperparameters\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| hidden_dim | 6144 |\n| num_layers | 48 |\n| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |\n| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |\n| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |\n| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |\n| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |\n| vocab_size | 128,256 |\n| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |\n| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |\n| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |\n| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |\n| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |\n| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |\n\n### Features\nAll structural (always on) unless noted.\n- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.\n- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.\n- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.\n- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).\n- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)\n- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.\n- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.\n- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).\n- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.\n- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).\n- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.\n- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).\n- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.\n- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.\n- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.\n- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.\n- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.\n\n## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)\n\nThree groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:\n- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.\n- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.\n- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.\n\n### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |\n| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |\n| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |\n| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |\n| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |\n| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |\n| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |\n| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |\n| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |\n\nThe MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.\n\n## 3. Training \u0026 topology\n- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.\n- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.\n- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).\n- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.\n- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).\n\n## 4. MFU / performance optimizations\n- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)\n- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.\n- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.\n- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.\n- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation=\"xla_fast_bwd\"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.\n- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.\n- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.\n- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.\n- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.\n- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:\n  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.\n  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.\n  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.\n- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.\n- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.\n- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.\n- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)\n- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.\n\n## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)\nRuns at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.\n\n| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |\n| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |\n| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |\n| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |\n| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |\n\n## 6.    124	
   125	class ExpertA2aParams(NamedTuple):
   126	    """Offset/size vectors for one direction of an expert-granular ``ragged_all_to_all``."""
   127	
   128	    input_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   129	    send_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   130	    output_offsets: Int[Array, "U"]
   131	    recv_sizes: Int[Array, "U"]
   132	
   133	
   134	def _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   135	    all_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   136	    clipped_group_sizes: Int[Array, "S E"],
   137	    shard_id: Int[Array, ""],
   138	    *,
   139	    local_expert_size: int,
   140	) -> tuple[ExpertA2aParams, ExpertA2aParams]:
   141	    """Build dispatch and return ``ragged_all_to_all`` parameters at (peer, expert) granularity.
   142	
   143	    One update per (destination shard, local expert). Sender reads each global-expert
   144	    group at its *unclipped* offset with its *clipped* size, so accepted rows need no
   145	    compaction: they are the prefix of each group. Receiver offsets pack arriving rows
   146	    expert-major (sender-major within each expert), so the received buffer needs no local
   147	    permute before the grouped MLP. The return direction is the exact mirror: it reads the
   148	    expert-major receiver buffer and writes valid prefixes back to the sender's unclipped
   149	    positions, leaving dropped rows at the output operand's values.
   150	    """
   151	    num_shards = all_group_sizes.shape[0]
   152	
   153	    # [src, dest, e]: rows sender `src` contributes to `dest`'s local expert `e`.
   154	    clipped = clipped_group_sizes.reshape(num_shards, num_shards, local_expert_size)
   155	
   156	    # Sender side: unclipped group starts in this shard's expert-sorted buffer.
   157	    unclipped_starts = jnp.cumsum(all_group_sizes, axis=1) - all_group_sizes
   158	    my_send = clipped[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   159	    dispatch_input_offsets = unclipped_starts[shard_id].reshape(num_shards, local_expert_size)
   160	
   161	    # Receiver side: expert-major segment starts on each destination, sender-major within.
   162	    dest_totals = jnp.sum(clipped, axis=0)  # [dest, e]
   163	    expert_starts = jnp.cumsum(dest_totals, axis=1) - dest_totals
   164	    senders_before_me = (jnp.cumsum(clipped, axis=0) - clipped)[shard_id]  # [dest, e]
   165	    dispatch_output_offsets = expert_starts + senders_before_me
   166	
   167	    # What each source sends this shard, source-major -- also the return direction's sends.
   168	    inbound = clipped[:, shard_id, :]  # [src, e]
   169	
   170	    dispatch = ExpertA2aParams(
   171	        dispatch_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   172	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   173	        dispatch_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   174	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   175	    )
   176	
   177	    # Return: read this shard's expert-major receiver buffer, write back to each original
   178	    # sender's unclipped sorted positions for the experts this shard owns.
   179	    my_expert_starts = expert_starts[shard_id]  # [e]
   180	    senders_before = jnp.cumsum(inbound, axis=0) - inbound  # [src, e]
   181	    return_input_offsets = my_expert_starts[None, :] + senders_before
   182	    my_global_experts = jnp.arange(local_expert_size, dtype=jnp.int32) + shard_id * local_expert_size
   183	    return_output_offsets = unclipped_starts[:, my_global_experts]  # [src, e]
   184	
   185	    ret = ExpertA2aParams(
   186	        return_input_offsets.reshape(-1),
   187	        inbound.reshape(-1),
   188	        return_output_offsets.reshape(-1),
   189	        my_send.reshape(-1),
   190	    )
   191	    return dispatch, ret

     4	"""cuDNN Frontend grouped weight gradients through the CuTeDSL JAX bridge."""
     5	
     6	import functools
     7	import importlib
     8	from typing import Any, NamedTuple
     9	
    10	import jax
    11	import jax.numpy as jnp
    12	
    13	from levanter.cutlass_kernel_cache import cute_launcher_factory, cutlass_call
    14	
    15	# Row count each expert group is padded up to, so every group starts where the kernel's
    16	# tile loads expect it to.
    17	#
    18	# This MUST match the kernel's own `FIX_PAD_SIZE`. cuDNN Frontend's grouped-Wgrad contract
    19	# requires every expert's token count to be divisible by this, and the kernel does not check:
    20	# it derives its per-expert tile count as `ceil(tokens_i / cta_tile_k)` while addressing through
    21	# one TMA descriptor over the whole buffer, so a group whose row count is not a multiple of the
    22	# tile reads its successor's rows as if they were its own and silently returns a wrong weight
    23	# gradient. `_assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel` pins this to the installed kernel so the
    24	# value cannot drift again (it was 8 here against a 256-row contract, which corrupted dw13 and
    25	# dw2 for every expert but the last in each call -- see issue #8339).
    26	_GROUP_ALIGNMENT = 256
    27	# Vector width the feature (non-grouped) dimensions must divide, which is what the tensor
    28	# specs below declare to the kernel.
    29	_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT = 8
    30	_MMA_TILER_MN = (256, 256)
    31	_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN = (2, 1)
    32	
    33	
    34	class _CudnnModules(NamedTuple):
    35	    """CuTeDSL and cuDNN Frontend entry points, imported only where the GPU extra exists."""
    36	
    37	    cutlass: Any
    38	    cute: Any
    39	    cutlass_jax: Any
    40	    kernel_type: Any
    41	    weight_mode: Any
    42	    input_order: Any
    43	
    44	
    45	@functools.cache
    46	def _cudnn_modules() -> _CudnnModules:
    47	    kernel_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.wgrad.moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad")
    48	    utility_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.moe_utils")
    49	    return _CudnnModules(
    50	        cutlass=importlib.import_module("cutlass"),
    51	        cute=importlib.import_module("cutlass.cute"),
    52	        cutlass_jax=importlib.import_module("cutlass.jax"),
    53	        kernel_type=kernel_module.MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel,
    54	        weight_mode=utility_module.MoEWeightMode,
    55	        input_order=utility_module.WGradInputOrder,
    56	    )
    57	
    58	
    59	def _assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel() -> None:
    60	    """Fail loudly if the installed kernel's required padding differs from `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT`.
    61	
    62	    The kernel silently returns wrong gradients when its groups are misaligned, so a mismatch
    63	    here has to raise rather than degrade.
    64	    """
    65	    required = getattr(_cudnn_modules().kernel_type, "FIX_PAD_SIZE", None)
    66	    if required is not None and required != _GROUP_ALIGNMENT:
    67	        raise RuntimeError(
    68	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad pads groups to {_GROUP_ALIGNMENT} rows but the installed kernel "
    69	            f"requires {required}. Misaligned groups are computed silently wrong, so refusing to run."
    70	        )
    71	
    72	
    73	@cute_launcher_factory
    74	def _build_launcher(
    75	    modules,
    76	    *,
    77	    expert_count: int,
    78	    max_active_clusters: int,
    79	):
    80	    @modules.cute.jit
    81	    def launcher(stream, mat_a, mat_b, offsets, output, workspace):
    82	        kernel = modules.kernel_type(
    83	            acc_dtype=modules.cutlass.Float32,
    84	            use_2cta_instrs=True,
    85	            mma_tiler_mn=_MMA_TILER_MN,
    86	            cluster_shape_mn=_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN,
    87	            accumulate_on_output=False,
    88	            expert_cnt=expert_count,
    89	            weight_mode=modules.weight_mode.DENSE,
    90	            input_order=modules.input_order.Tensor2D,
    91	        )
    92	        kernel(mat_a, mat_b, output, offsets, workspace, max_active_clusters, stream, None)
    93	
    94	    return launcher

    96	
    97	def pad_grouped_rows(values: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array]:
    98	    """Insert zero rows so each contiguous expert group ends on a `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` boundary."""
    99	    if values.ndim != 2:
   100	        raise ValueError(f"values must be rank 2, got shape={values.shape}")
   101	    if values.shape[0] == 0:
   102	        raise ValueError("values must contain at least one physical row")
   103	    if group_sizes.ndim != 1 or group_sizes.shape[0] == 0:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"group_sizes must be a nonempty vector, got shape={group_sizes.shape}")
   105	
   106	    group_sizes = group_sizes.astype(jnp.int32)
   107	    padded_group_sizes = ((group_sizes + _GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) // _GROUP_ALIGNMENT) * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
   108	    active_offsets = jnp.cumsum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   109	    padded_offsets = jnp.cumsum(padded_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   110	    active_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), active_offsets[:-1]])
   111	    padded_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), padded_offsets[:-1]])
   112	
   113	    # At most `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1` rows are inserted per group. Keep a static worst-case tail so
   114	    # the output shape does not depend on the runtime routing counts.
   115	    padded_capacity = values.shape[0] + (_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) * group_sizes.shape[0]
   116	    padded_rows = jnp.arange(padded_capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
   117	    expert_ids = jnp.sum(padded_rows[:, None] >= padded_offsets[None, :], axis=1, dtype=jnp.int32)
   118	    safe_expert_ids = jnp.minimum(expert_ids, group_sizes.shape[0] - 1)
   119	    rows_within_group = padded_rows - padded_starts[safe_expert_ids]
   120	    source_rows = active_starts[safe_expert_ids] + rows_within_group
   121	    valid = (expert_ids < group_sizes.shape[0]) & (rows_within_group < group_sizes[safe_expert_ids])
   122	    source_rows = jnp.clip(source_rows, 0, values.shape[0] - 1)
   123	    padded = jnp.where(valid[:, None], values[source_rows], jnp.zeros((), dtype=values.dtype))
   124	    return padded, padded_offsets
   125	
   126	
   127	def cudnn_grouped_wgrad(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
   128	    """Compute per-expert ``lhs.T @ rhs`` for contiguous ragged row groups."""
   129	    _assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel()
   130	    if lhs.ndim != 2 or rhs.ndim != 2:
   131	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs must be rank 2, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   132	    if lhs.shape[0] != rhs.shape[0]:
   133	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs row counts must match, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   134	    if lhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16 or rhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16:
   135	        raise ValueError(f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad requires BF16 inputs, got lhs={lhs.dtype}, rhs={rhs.dtype}")
   136	    if lhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0 or rhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   137	        raise ValueError(
   138	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad feature dimensions must divide {_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT}, "
   139	            f"got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}"
   140	        )
   141	
   142	    lhs_padded, padded_offsets = pad_grouped_rows(lhs, group_sizes)
   143	    rhs_padded, _ = pad_grouped_rows(rhs, group_sizes)
   144	    modules = _cudnn_modules()
   145	    max_active_clusters = modules.cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters(
   146	        _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[0] * _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[1]
   147	    )
   148	    launcher = _build_launcher(
   149	        modules,
   150	        expert_count=group_sizes.shape[0],
   151	        max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
   152	    )
   153	    tensor_spec = modules.cutlass_jax.TensorSpec
   154	    call = cutlass_call(
   155	        launcher,
   156	        output_shape_dtype=(
   157	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((group_sizes.shape[0], lhs.shape[1], rhs.shape[1]), lhs.dtype),
   158	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1,), jnp.uint8),
   159	        ),
   160	        input_spec=(
   161	            tensor_spec(mode=(1, 0), divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   162	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   163	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   164	        ),
   165	        output_spec=(
   166	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, 1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   167	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   168	        ),
   169	        use_static_tensors=False,
   170	    )
   171	    output, _workspace = call(lhs_padded, rhs_padded, padded_offsets)
   172	    return output
    90	
    91	
    92	@jax.custom_vjp
    93	def _expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
    94	    """``_expert_mlp`` with the two weight-gradient GEMMs on cuDNN grouped Wgrad kernels.
    95	
    96	    The forward output is masked past the last expert group: the grouped GEMMs write only
    97	    the rows inside ``cu``, and those trailing rows flow on through the unpermute and
    98	    combine, so they have to be zero rather than whatever the buffer held.
    99	    """
   100	    _gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   101	    y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   102	    return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu)
   103	
   104	
   105	def _expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu):
   106	    gu, h = quack_gated_grouped_gemm(x_dispatch, w13_il, cu, return_preact=True, **_QUACK_GATED_KW)
   107	    y = quack_grouped_gemm(h, moe_w2, cu, b_major="n", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   108	    return _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(y, cu), (x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu)
   109	
   110	
   111	def _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd(res, dy):
   112	    x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, gu, h, group_sizes, cu = res
   113	    # The cotangent's trailing rows are whatever the caller's buffer held; the grouped GEMMs
   114	    # contract every row they are handed, so they have to be cleared here too.
   115	    dy = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dy, cu)
   116	    dh = quack_grouped_gemm(dy, moe_w2, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   117	    dw2 = cudnn_grouped_wgrad(h, dy, group_sizes)
   118	    d_gu = _swiglu_gate_up_backward(gu, dh)
   119	    dx = quack_grouped_gemm(d_gu, w13_il, cu, b_major="k", **_QUACK_GROUPED_KW)
   120	    dx = _zero_inactive_grouped_rows(dx, cu)
   121	    dw13_il = cudnn_grouped_wgrad(x_dispatch, d_gu, group_sizes)
   122	    gs_ct = np.zeros(group_sizes.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   123	    cu_ct = np.zeros(cu.shape, dtype=jax.dtypes.float0)
   124	    return dx, dw13_il, dw2, gs_ct, cu_ct
   125	
   126	
   127	_expert_mlp_cudnn.defvjp(_expert_mlp_cudnn_fwd, _expert_mlp_cudnn_bwd)
   128

   130	def _moe_mlp_local_sonic_cute(
   131	    x: Float[Array, "T H"],
   132	    selected_experts: Int[Array, "T K"],
   133	    combine_weights: Float[Array, "T K"],
   134	    moe_w13: Float[Array, "E H I2"],
   135	    moe_w2: Float[Array, "E I H"],
   136	    *,
   137	    num_experts: int,
   138	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T H"], Int[Array, ""]]:
   139	    x_dispatch, w_dispatch, token_dispatch, group_sizes = _prepare_moe_dispatch(
   140	        x, selected_experts, combine_weights, num_experts=num_experts
   141	    )
   142	    x_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(x_dispatch, _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_INPUT)
   143	    moe_dim = moe_w2.shape[1]
   144	    w13_il = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13, moe_dim)
   145	    cu = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)])
   146	
   147	    with jax.named_scope("moe_up_down_quack"):
   148	        out_dispatch = tree_checkpoint_name(
   149	            _expert_mlp(x_dispatch, w13_il, moe_w2, group_sizes, cu), _CHECKPOINT_DISPATCH_OUTPUT
   150	        )
   151	
   152	    with jax.named_scope("scatter"):
   153	        out = jnp.zeros_like(x).at[token_dispatch].add(out_dispatch * w_dispatch[:, None], mode="drop")
   154	    return out, _zero_dropped_assignments()

     4	"""cuDNN Frontend grouped weight gradients through the CuTeDSL JAX bridge."""
     5	
     6	import functools
     7	import importlib
     8	from typing import Any, NamedTuple

    13	from levanter.cutlass_kernel_cache import cute_launcher_factory, cutlass_call
    14	
    15	# Row count each expert group is padded up to, so every group starts where the kernel's
    16	# tile loads expect it to.
    17	#
    18	# This MUST match the kernel's own `FIX_PAD_SIZE`. cuDNN Frontend's grouped-Wgrad contract
    19	# requires every expert's token count to be divisible by this, and the kernel does not check:
    20	# it derives its per-expert tile count as `ceil(tokens_i / cta_tile_k)` while addressing through
    21	# one TMA descriptor over the whole buffer, so a group whose row count is not a multiple of the
    22	# tile reads its successor's rows as if they were its own and silently returns a wrong weight
    23	# gradient. `_assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel` pins this to the installed kernel so the
    24	# value cannot drift again (it was 8 here against a 256-row contract, which corrupted dw13 and
    25	# dw2 for every expert but the last in each call -- see issue #8339).
    26	_GROUP_ALIGNMENT = 256
    27	# Vector width the feature (non-grouped) dimensions must divide, which is what the tensor
    28	# specs below declare to the kernel.
    29	_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT = 8
    30	_MMA_TILER_MN = (256, 256)
    31	_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN = (2, 1)
    32	
    33	
    34	class _CudnnModules(NamedTuple):
    35	    """CuTeDSL and cuDNN Frontend entry points, imported only where the GPU extra exists."""
    36	
    37	    cutlass: Any
    38	    cute: Any
    39	    cutlass_jax: Any
    40	    kernel_type: Any
    41	    weight_mode: Any
    42	    input_order: Any
    43

    45	@functools.cache
    46	def _cudnn_modules() -> _CudnnModules:
    47	    kernel_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.wgrad.moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad")
    48	    utility_module = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.moe_utils")
    49	    return _CudnnModules(
    50	        cutlass=importlib.import_module("cutlass"),
    51	        cute=importlib.import_module("cutlass.cute"),
    52	        cutlass_jax=importlib.import_module("cutlass.jax"),
    53	        kernel_type=kernel_module.MoEGroupedGemmWgradBF16Kernel,
    54	        weight_mode=utility_module.MoEWeightMode,
    55	        input_order=utility_module.WGradInputOrder,
    56	    )

    59	def _assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel() -> None:
    60	    """Fail loudly if the installed kernel's required padding differs from `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT`.
    61	
    62	    The kernel silently returns wrong gradients when its groups are misaligned, so a mismatch
    63	    here has to raise rather than degrade.
    64	    """
    65	    required = getattr(_cudnn_modules().kernel_type, "FIX_PAD_SIZE", None)
    66	    if required is not None and required != _GROUP_ALIGNMENT:
    67	        raise RuntimeError(
    68	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad pads groups to {_GROUP_ALIGNMENT} rows but the installed kernel "
    69	            f"requires {required}. Misaligned groups are computed silently wrong, so refusing to run."
    70	        )
    71

    73	@cute_launcher_factory
    74	def _build_launcher(
    75	    modules,
    76	    *,
    77	    expert_count: int,
    78	    max_active_clusters: int,
    79	):
    80	    @modules.cute.jit
    81	    def launcher(stream, mat_a, mat_b, offsets, output, workspace):
    82	        kernel = modules.kernel_type(
    83	            acc_dtype=modules.cutlass.Float32,
    84	            use_2cta_instrs=True,
    85	            mma_tiler_mn=_MMA_TILER_MN,
    86	            cluster_shape_mn=_CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN,
    87	            accumulate_on_output=False,
    88	            expert_cnt=expert_count,
    89	            weight_mode=modules.weight_mode.DENSE,
    90	            input_order=modules.input_order.Tensor2D,
    91	        )
    92	        kernel(mat_a, mat_b, output, offsets, workspace, max_active_clusters, stream, None)
    93	
    94	    return launcher

    97	def pad_grouped_rows(values: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> tuple[jax.Array, jax.Array]:
    98	    """Insert zero rows so each contiguous expert group ends on a `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT` boundary."""
    99	    if values.ndim != 2:
   100	        raise ValueError(f"values must be rank 2, got shape={values.shape}")
   101	    if values.shape[0] == 0:
   102	        raise ValueError("values must contain at least one physical row")
   103	    if group_sizes.ndim != 1 or group_sizes.shape[0] == 0:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"group_sizes must be a nonempty vector, got shape={group_sizes.shape}")
   105	
   106	    group_sizes = group_sizes.astype(jnp.int32)
   107	    padded_group_sizes = ((group_sizes + _GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) // _GROUP_ALIGNMENT) * _GROUP_ALIGNMENT
   108	    active_offsets = jnp.cumsum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   109	    padded_offsets = jnp.cumsum(padded_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   110	    active_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), active_offsets[:-1]])
   111	    padded_starts = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), padded_offsets[:-1]])
   112	
   113	    # At most `_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1` rows are inserted per group. Keep a static worst-case tail so
   114	    # the output shape does not depend on the runtime routing counts.
   115	    padded_capacity = values.shape[0] + (_GROUP_ALIGNMENT - 1) * group_sizes.shape[0]
   116	    padded_rows = jnp.arange(padded_capacity, dtype=jnp.int32)
   117	    expert_ids = jnp.sum(padded_rows[:, None] >= padded_offsets[None, :], axis=1, dtype=jnp.int32)
   118	    safe_expert_ids = jnp.minimum(expert_ids, group_sizes.shape[0] - 1)
   119	    rows_within_group = padded_rows - padded_starts[safe_expert_ids]
   120	    source_rows = active_starts[safe_expert_ids] + rows_within_group
   121	    valid = (expert_ids < group_sizes.shape[0]) & (rows_within_group < group_sizes[safe_expert_ids])
   122	    source_rows = jnp.clip(source_rows, 0, values.shape[0] - 1)
   123	    padded = jnp.where(valid[:, None], values[source_rows], jnp.zeros((), dtype=values.dtype))
   124	    return padded, padded_offsets
   125

   127	def cudnn_grouped_wgrad(lhs: jax.Array, rhs: jax.Array, group_sizes: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
   128	    """Compute per-expert ``lhs.T @ rhs`` for contiguous ragged row groups."""
   129	    _assert_group_alignment_matches_kernel()
   130	    if lhs.ndim != 2 or rhs.ndim != 2:
   131	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs must be rank 2, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   132	    if lhs.shape[0] != rhs.shape[0]:
   133	        raise ValueError(f"lhs and rhs row counts must match, got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}")
   134	    if lhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16 or rhs.dtype != jnp.bfloat16:
   135	        raise ValueError(f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad requires BF16 inputs, got lhs={lhs.dtype}, rhs={rhs.dtype}")
   136	    if lhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0 or rhs.shape[1] % _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT != 0:
   137	        raise ValueError(
   138	            f"cuDNN grouped Wgrad feature dimensions must divide {_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT}, "
   139	            f"got lhs={lhs.shape}, rhs={rhs.shape}"
   140	        )
   141	
   142	    lhs_padded, padded_offsets = pad_grouped_rows(lhs, group_sizes)
   143	    rhs_padded, _ = pad_grouped_rows(rhs, group_sizes)
   144	    modules = _cudnn_modules()
   145	    max_active_clusters = modules.cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters(
   146	        _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[0] * _CLUSTER_SHAPE_MN[1]
   147	    )
   148	    launcher = _build_launcher(
   149	        modules,
   150	        expert_count=group_sizes.shape[0],
   151	        max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
   152	    )
   153	    tensor_spec = modules.cutlass_jax.TensorSpec
   154	    call = cutlass_call(
   155	        launcher,
   156	        output_shape_dtype=(
   157	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((group_sizes.shape[0], lhs.shape[1], rhs.shape[1]), lhs.dtype),
   158	            jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1,), jnp.uint8),
   159	        ),
   160	        input_spec=(
   161	            tensor_spec(mode=(1, 0), divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   162	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   163	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   164	        ),
   165	        output_spec=(
   166	            tensor_spec(divisibility=(1, 1, _FEATURE_ALIGNMENT), static=False),
   167	            tensor_spec(static=False),
   168	        ),
   169	        use_static_tensors=False,
   170	    )
   171	    output, _workspace = call(lhs_padded, rhs_padded, padded_offsets)
   172	    return output

    71	class _ExpertMlp(Protocol):
    72	    """Runs the expert MLP over a receiver buffer laid out expert-major.
    73	
    74	    Implementations take both views of the buffer's group sizes: the physical sizes, which charge
    75	    trailing padding to the last expert, and the active sizes, which count only received rows.
    76	    Which one a kernel reads depends on whether it covers the whole buffer or works from segment
    77	    boundaries, so both are always passed and a kernel discards the one it does not use.
    78	    """
    79	
    80	    def __call__(
    81	        self,
    82	        x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
    83	        moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    84	        moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    85	        physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    86	        active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    87	        activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
    88	    ) -> Float[Array, "C H"]: ...
    89	
    90	
    91	def _ragged_dot_expert_mlp(
    92	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
    93	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
    94	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
    95	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    96	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
    97	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
    98	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
    99	    """Portable expert MLP over XLA's `ragged_dot`, which covers the whole receiver buffer."""
   100	    del active_group_sizes
   101	    w13_out = ragged_dot(x_dispatch, moe_w13_local, physical_group_sizes)
   102	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   103	    gate, up = jnp.split(w13_out, [moe_dim], axis=-1)
   104	    return ragged_dot(activation_fn(gate) * up, moe_w2_local, physical_group_sizes)
   105	
   106	
   107	def _cute_expert_mlp(
   108	    x_dispatch: Float[Array, "C H"],
   109	    moe_w13_local: Float[Array, "Echunk H I2"],
   110	    moe_w2_local: Float[Array, "Echunk I H"],
   111	    physical_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   112	    active_group_sizes: Int[Array, "Echunk"],
   113	    activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array],
   114	) -> Float[Array, "C H"]:
   115	    """Expert MLP on QuACK's SM100 grouped GEMMs plus cuDNN grouped weight gradients.
   116	
   117	    The grouped kernels are driven by segment boundaries, so they take the active sizes and
   118	    mask the receiver buffer's trailing padding rather than charging it to the last expert.
   119	    """
   120	    del activation_fn, physical_group_sizes
   121	
   122	    # QuACK, cuDNN Frontend, and CUTLASS DSL are installed only with the CUDA 13 GPU extra.
   123	    from levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute import _expert_mlp_cudnn  # noqa: PLC0415
   124	
   125	    moe_dim = moe_w2_local.shape[1]
   126	    w13_interleaved = _interleave_gate_up(moe_w13_local, moe_dim)
   127	    cumulative_group_sizes = jnp.concatenate(
   128	        [jnp.zeros((1,), jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(active_group_sizes).astype(jnp.int32)]
   129	    )
   130	    return _expert_mlp_cudnn(x_dispatch, w13_interleaved, moe_w2_local, active_group_sizes, cumulative_group_sizes)
   131	
   132	
   133	@functools.cache
   134	def _quack_grouped_gemm_available() -> bool:
   135	    if jax.default_backend() != "gpu":
   136	        return False
   137	    if float(jax.devices("gpu")[0].compute_capability) < _SM100_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY:
   138	        return False
   139	    try:
   140	        import levanter.grug._moe.sonic_cute  # noqa: F401,PLC0415
   141	        from levanter.grug._moe.cudnn_wgrad_cute import _cudnn_modules  # noqa: PLC0415
   142	
   143	        _ = _cudnn_modules()  # check if compatible cudnn is available
   144	    except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
   145	        logger.warning(
   146	            "SM100 GPU present but the QuACK/cuDNN grouped-GEMM kernels did not import (%s). "
   147	            "The ragged expert MLP falls back to ragged_dot, which computes the same function "
   148	            "more slowly. Install levanter's `gpu` extra to use them.",
   149	            exc,
   150	        )
   151	        return False
   152	    return True
   153	
   154	
   155	def _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn: Callable[[jax.Array], jax.Array]) -> _ExpertMlp:
   156	    """Pick the fastest expert-MLP kernel this process can actually run.
   157	
   158	    QuACK's kernel fuses SwiGLU, so it only applies to SiLU. Everything else -- another
   159	    activation, a non-SM100 GPU, a TPU or CPU, or a build without the GPU extra -- runs the
   160	    portable `ragged_dot` path, which computes the same function.
   161	    """
   162	    if activation_fn is jax.nn.silu and _quack_grouped_gemm_available():
   163	        return _cute_expert_mlp
   164	    return _ragged_dot_expert_mlp
   165	
   166	
   167	def _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   168	    intermediate: Float[Array, "TK H"],
   169	    sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"],
   170	    combine_weights_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal K"],
   171	    *,
   172	    tokens_per_shard: int,
   173	    topk: int,
   174	) -> Float[Array, "Tlocal H"]:
   175	    """Weight each token's expert outputs by its routing weights and sum them."""
   176	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices)
   177	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   178	        # One kernel for the gather and the sum, materializing neither the unpermuted
   179	        # ``[TK, H]`` buffer nor the ``[T, K, H]`` view -- at top-8 that view is eight times
   180	        # the output. It accumulates in fp32 like the einsum below and keeps the routing
   181	        # weight in fp32 through the multiply, where the einsum has to cast it down to avoid
   182	        # promoting the larger operand, so the two agree to a single rounding.
   183	        return sonic_gather_sum(intermediate, positions.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk), combine_weights_local)
   184	    unsorted = _sort_activations(intermediate, positions)
   185	    reshaped = unsorted.reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk, -1)
   186	    return jnp.einsum(
   187	        "tkd,tk->td", reshaped, combine_weights_local.astype(reshaped.dtype), preferred_element_type=jnp.float32
   188	    )
   189	
   190	
   191	@functools.partial(jax.custom_vjp, nondiff_argnums=(2,))
   192	def _gather_dispatch_rows(
   193	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   194	) -> Float[Array, "TK H"]:
   195	    """Build the expert-sorted dispatch buffer with one gather.
   196	
   197	    Equivalent to ``jnp.repeat(x_local, topk, axis=0)[sorted_indices]`` without
   198	    materializing the repeated buffer or running a data-sized permute. The backward pass
   199	    is the transpose: each token sums the cotangent rows of its ``topk`` sorted slots.
   200	    """
   201	    return x_local[sorted_indices // topk]
   202	
   203	
   204	def _gather_dispatch_rows_fwd(
   205	    x_local: Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], topk: int
   206	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "TK H"], Int[Array, "TK"]]:
   207	    return _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk), sorted_indices
   208	
   209	
   210	def _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd(
   211	    topk: int, sorted_indices: Int[Array, "TK"], cotangent: Float[Array, "TK H"]
   212	) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tlocal H"], None]:
   213	    tokens_per_shard = sorted_indices.shape[0] // topk
   214	    positions = jnp.argsort(sorted_indices).reshape(tokens_per_shard, topk)
   215	    if sonic_gather_sum_available():
   216	        ones = jnp.ones((tokens_per_shard, topk), dtype=jnp.float32)
   217	        grad_x = sonic_gather_sum(cotangent, positions, ones)
   218	    else:
   219	        grad_x = jnp.sum(cotangent[positions], axis=1, dtype=jnp.float32)
   220	    return grad_x.astype(cotangent.dtype), None
   221	
   222	
   223	_gather_dispatch_rows.defvjp(_gather_dispatch_rows_fwd, _gather_dispatch_rows_bwd)
   224	
   225	
   226	def _loop_local_zeros(
   227	    rows: int, hidden_dim: int, dtype, tie: Int[Array, "..."], site: int = 0
   228	) -> Float[Array, "rows H"]:
   229	    """Zero buffer for an in-place ``ragged_all_to_all`` output slot, built so XLA never copies it.
   230	
   430	    # makes drop clipping per-chunk, which is a routing difference, not just a memory one.
   431	    #
   432	    # What chunking does not change is what crosses the forward/backward boundary. The block's
   433	    # remat policy re-runs this function in the backward, so the lowered module carries every
   434	    # ragged all-to-all three times at any chunk count -- primal, backward recompute, transpose,
   435	    # verified in the lowered StableHLO: 12 ops at two chunks, 6 at one. The a2a outputs are
   436	    # transient inside a chunk, not residuals pinned across the block window.
   437	    chunks = _resolve_expert_chunks(expert_chunks, local_experts)
   438	    chunk_experts = local_experts // chunks
   439	    chunk_capacity = max(chunk_experts, int(math.ceil(local_capacity / chunks)))
   440	    hidden_dim = x_local.shape[1]
   441	
   442	    with jax.named_scope("dispatch"):
   443	        flat_selected = selected_experts_local.reshape(-1)  # [TK]
   444	        sorted_indices = tree_checkpoint_name(jnp.argsort(flat_selected), RAGGED_SORTED_INDICES_REMAT_NAME)  # [TK]
   445	        group_sizes = tree_checkpoint_name(
   446	            jnp.bincount(flat_selected, length=num_experts).astype(jnp.int32), RAGGED_GROUP_SIZES_REMAT_NAME
   447	        )  # [E]
   448	        sorted_x = _gather_dispatch_rows(x_local, sorted_indices, topk)  # [TK, H]
   449	        all_group_sizes = jax.lax.all_gather(group_sizes, "expert")  # [S, E]
   450	
   451	    expert_mlp = _select_expert_mlp(activation_fn)
   452	    chunk_of_expert = (jnp.arange(num_experts, dtype=jnp.int32) % local_experts) // chunk_experts  # [E]
   453	    # Built per-iteration (not jnp.zeros) so the layer scan does not re-copy a hoisted
   454	    # constant into the in-place return a2a's output slot every step; see _loop_local_zeros.
   455	    # The zeros are load-bearing: rows no peer writes back must read 0 in the combine.
   456	    returned = _loop_local_zeros(assignments_per_shard, hidden_dim, x_local.dtype, group_sizes, site=5)  # [TK, H]
   457	    accepted_local = jnp.zeros((), dtype=jnp.int32)
   458	    for chunk_index in range(chunks):
   459	        with jax.named_scope(f"moe_chunk_{chunk_index}"):
   460	            chunk_all_group_sizes = jnp.where(chunk_of_expert[None, :] == chunk_index, all_group_sizes, 0)  # [S, E]
   461	            clipped_group_sizes = _clip_receiver_group_sizes(
   462	                chunk_all_group_sizes,
   463	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   464	                receiver_capacity=chunk_capacity,
   465	            )
   466	            # Sender starts come from the full (unmasked) sizes, so each chunk reads its
   467	            # groups' accepted prefixes in place in the shared sorted buffer.
   468	            dispatch_params, return_params = _expert_granular_a2a_params(
   469	                all_group_sizes,
   470	                clipped_group_sizes,
   471	                shard_id,
   472	                local_expert_size=local_experts,
   473	            )
   474	            # Serialize the chunks. Without this barrier, the scheduler can start the dispatch
   475	            # of every chunk at the same time. This causes the high memory use that the chunks
   476	            # prevent. A variant that overlaps one transport with the MLP stays within memory.
   477	            # But it does not increase the speed. The transport and the MLP compete for the
   478	            # same SMs.
   479	            chunk_source, _ = jax.lax.optimization_barrier((sorted_x, returned))
   480	            # Accepted rows are the prefix of each unclipped expert group and receiver offsets
   481	            # pack arrivals expert-major, so the received buffer feeds the grouped MLP
   482	            # directly: no sender compaction and no receiver-side permute.
   483	            x_dispatch = _dispatch_ragged_a2a(  # [C, H]
   484	                chunk_capacity,
   485	                assignments_per_shard,
   486	                chunk_source,
   487	                *dispatch_params,
   488	            )
   489	            active_all = jnp.sum(  # [Elocal]
   490	                clipped_group_sizes.reshape(ep_size, ep_size, local_experts)[:, shard_id, :], axis=0
   491	            )
   492	            active_group_sizes = active_all[
   493	                chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts
   494	            ]  # [Echunk]
   495	            total_valid = jnp.sum(active_group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32)
   496	            physical_group_sizes = active_group_sizes.at[-1].add(chunk_capacity - total_valid)  # [Echunk]
   497	            out_dispatch = expert_mlp(  # [C, H]
   498	                x_dispatch,
   499	                moe_w13_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   500	                moe_w2_local[chunk_index * chunk_experts : (chunk_index + 1) * chunk_experts],
   501	                physical_group_sizes,
   502	                active_group_sizes,
   503	                activation_fn,
   504	            )
   505	            # The mirror of dispatch: valid prefixes land back at unclipped sorted positions.
   506	            # Chaining every chunk through one output buffer composes the disjoint writes;
   507	            # dropped rows keep the buffer's zeros, so the final gather-sum reads dropped
   508	            # slots as zero contributions with no expansion step.
   509	            returned = _return_ragged_a2a(
   510	                chunk_capacity,
   511	                out_dispatch,
   512	                returned,
   513	                *return_params,
   514	            )
   515	            accepted_local = accepted_local + jnp.sum(clipped_group_sizes[shard_id], dtype=jnp.int32)
   516	
   517	    with jax.named_scope("combine"):
   518	        out_local = _unpermute_from_global_expert(
   519	            returned,
   520	            sorted_indices,
   521	            combine_weights_local,
   522	            tokens_per_shard=tokens_per_shard,
   523	            topk=topk,
   524	        ).astype(x_local.dtype)
   525	        dropped_local = jnp.sum(group_sizes, dtype=jnp.int32) - accepted_local
   526	        dropped_total = jax.lax.psum(dropped_local, _batch_axes(jax.sharding.get_abstract_mesh()))
   527	    return out_local, CapacityOverflow(sender=dropped_total, receiver=jnp.zeros_like(dropped_total))

# Marin House Style

Read the medium-specific guide for the deliverable, then apply
[ai-writing-donts.md](ai-writing-donts.md) as the final prose pass.

## Read The Right File

- Read [blog-posts.md](blog-posts.md) for public explainers and blog posts.
- Read [reports.md](reports.md) for technical reports aimed at peer researchers outside Marin.
- Read [tutorials.md](tutorials.md) for learning-oriented documentation that introduces Marin.
- Read [reference-docs.md](reference-docs.md) for precise usage docs aimed at readers who already know Marin.
- Read [issues.md](issues.md) for standard OSS issues and experiment issues.
- Read [pull-requests.md](pull-requests.md) for commit messages and PR titles and bodies.
- Read [discord.md](discord.md) for Discord summaries and tactical replies.
- If a piece spans media, use the stricter applicable rule.

## Voice

Write as a rigorous open-science lab building foundation models. Treat
experiments, decisions, and mistakes as part of the record. Use a sober,
practical voice for technically capable peers. Be natural and direct; use
specialized language when it improves precision.

## On Voice

These rules are stricter for agents. Preserve harmless human flourishes when
editing another person's prose.

## Evidence and scope

- Lead with the result, decision, or changed behavior.
- Support claims with numbers, examples, observations, and relevant artifacts.
- State uncertainty and limitations plainly; do not imply broader evidence.
- Remove hype, product-announcement language, AGI speculation, decorative
  emoji, and adjectives standing in for evidence.
- Explain non-standard terms. Add detail only when it helps the reader
  reproduce, evaluate, or act.

## Add Structure For Longer-Form Writing

Long-form pieces may need a document-level TL;DR and section takeaways. Do not
force them into short media.

Before publishing, confirm the prose is factually current, sounds normal when
spoken to a colleague, cites material evidence, and contains no generic filler.

# AI-Writing Don'ts

Use this as the final prose pass for agent-written Marin text. Delete first.
Rewrite only when the sentence carries a fact, decision, result, constraint, or
caveat.

## Use Plain Technical English

Apply Orwell's rules of writing and Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100).
Prefer short, active sentences, common concrete words, one action or claim per
sentence, and one term for each concept. Cut words that add no fact. Avoid stale
metaphors and idioms. Keep specialized terms when they improve precision, and
explain unfamiliar terms. If a term's origin or exact meaning is unclear, omit
it or research it until you can explain it to other readers. Repeating jargon
solely because another source used it hides uncertainty and spreads undefined
language. Break a rule when following it would make the prose less clear or
accurate.

## Test With A Cold Reader

For durable prose or any text that must stand alone, give a context-less
subagent only the finished draft and its intended audience. Do not provide the
conversation, source notes, diff, or author intent. Ask what terms, referents,
claims, or causal links a first-time reader cannot recover from the text.
Fix concrete gaps with the smallest local edit. Extra context can hide the main
claim and overload a first-time reader. Narrow or reshape a claim when its full
explanation would interrupt the text; put optional background behind a link. Do
not add conversation history that the intended audience does not need, and do
not turn personal style preferences into findings.

## Cut Empty Sentences

Delete a sentence when removing it loses no information. Common waste:

- bridge prose: `The main change is...`, `Stepping back...`, `What this means is...`
- importance claims: `Importantly`, `It is worth noting`, `This is the key point`
- stage directions: `Let's dive in`, `Here is a summary`, `In this section...`
- effort narration: `After extensive investigation...`
- generic conclusions, recaps, future-work sections, and chatbot sign-offs
- prose that restates a heading, list length, table, diff, or visible structure

Start with the fact. End when the useful information ends.

## Ban Stock Contrast

Remove rhetorical templates built around a staged opposition:

- `X, not Y`
- `not X, but Y`
- `not just X, but also Y`
- `more than X`
- `the question is no longer X; it is Y`
- `the real story is X`
- `what matters is X`
- `rather than Y` when no real comparison is being made

State X directly. Split real comparisons into plain claims.

Bad:

> The issue is not query execution, but the metadata path.

Better:

> Metadata loading takes 12 seconds. Query execution takes 400 ms.

Bad:

> The change improves reliability, not just performance.

Better:

> Median latency fell 18%. Failed retries fell from 7 to 0.

Grammatical negation is fine when the negative fact matters: `The ablation has
not run.` A measured comparison is fine when both sides matter.

## Require Evidence

- Name the code path, configuration, issue, artifact, measurement, or unknown.
- Replace adjectives with evidence. Delete `robust`, `powerful`, `seamless`,
  `significant`, `crucial`, and `pivotal` unless a concrete result follows.
- Say `we have not tested X` when evidence is missing.
- Keep prose consistent with tables, code, and current behavior.
- Remove stale explanations after the implementation changes.
- Use one precise term for one technical object.

## Avoid LLM Cadence

- Skip adjective trios and forced rules of three.
- Skip `Additionally`, `Furthermore`, `Moreover`, `Importantly`, and `Notably`.
- Skip `landscape`, `ecosystem`, `interplay`, `tapestry`, `testament`, `delve`,
  `showcase`, `underscore`, and `foster`.
- Avoid em-dash asides. Make the point a sentence or delete it.
- Avoid bold labels, takeaway boxes, and decorative headings.
- Do not rotate synonyms for the same object.

## Score Every Paragraph

Each paragraph must contain a concrete result, setup, decision, constraint, or
caveat. Rewrite or delete paragraphs that only frame significance or smooth a
transition.

Ask of every sentence:

1. What information disappears if I delete it?
2. Can I replace it with a number, named fact, decision, or explicit unknown?
3. Does it still describe the current code and evidence?
4. Could it appear unchanged in a random software announcement?

Delete sentences that fail this check.

## Prefer Plain Rewrites

- `The main change is that retries are bounded.` → `Retries stop after five attempts.`
- `This highlights a scalability problem.` → `Registration takes 1.2 seconds for 100 workers.`
- `The current state is much clearer.` → Name the resolved and open questions.
- `This is procedural progress.` → `The code is ready. The ablation has not run.`
- `The configuration has three parts:` → Start the list.

Finish with a search for stock contrast, bridge phrases, unsupported adjectives,
and stale claims. Prefer a shorter accurate document.

# Reports

Use this file for technical reports and research writeups.

## Assume This Reader

- Assume the reader is a peer researcher working in the same general area.
- Do not assume the reader uses Marin or cares about Marin as a codebase.
- Assume the reader cares about the result, the experimental setup, and the high-level methodology.
- Do not assume familiarity with your specific method or terminology.

## Optimize For

- Give enough detail for someone to reproduce, critique, or extend the work in their own stack.
- Make the main result and methodological choice legible without forcing the reader through Marin-specific context.
- Preserve first-read clarity instead of chasing exhaustive completeness.

## Write This Way

- Lead with the result, then show how you got there, then state caveats.
- Include a doc-level TL;DR near the top.
- Add section-level takeaway lines when sections are long enough that readers need orientation.
- Define non-standard or ambiguous terms briefly before relying on them.
- Include concrete setup details, metrics, and comparison points.
- Describe methodology at the level needed for a peer to evaluate the work, not at the level of Marin implementation internals unless those internals matter to the result.
- Remove repo-local detail that does not help an outside researcher interpret the result.
- Link to repo internals when they help with reproduction or provide useful context (similar to an appendix in a paper).
- Clearly separate confirmed results from exploratory findings (e.g., label as exploratory, replicated, or stable).
- Cite the prior work that the report builds on or compares against, including relevant Marin experiments and external papers where appropriate.

## Test

- Ask whether a researcher in another codebase or organization could evaluate the work without outside context.

## Reconciled verdict

The verdict remains **incorrect for the ragged path on SM100 with SiLU and the QuACK/cuDNN expert MLP**.

Your correction changes the blast radius decisively. `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` uses `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`; its expert MLP is ordinary `jnp.einsum` and JAX autodiff ([source](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all.py:449)). It is outside this defect. This is a ragged-migration blocker, not a live incident in that run.

I would push back on “every ragged run” literally. The affected conditions are:

- SM100 or newer.
- SiLU selects `_cute_expert_mlp`.
- QuACK and cuDNN Frontend are available.
- A Wgrad call has a non-final group whose padded length is not a multiple of the internal 64-row K tile.

TPU, H100, other activations, missing GPU extras, and other cases that fall back to `ragged_dot` are unaffected. A one-expert call also reads only zero tail. The intended GB200 hero-shaped ragged migration satisfies the affected conditions throughout, so its practical blast radius is still broad.

## 1. Does the 40× split corroborate the defect?

Yes, strongly, but it is not a clean causal isolation.

Ring and ragged are intended to compute the same no-drop MoE function, but they differ in substantially more than transport:

- Ring uses `all_gather`/`psum_scatter` and `ragged_dot` for the expert forward and autodiff ([source](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:25)).
- Ragged uses ragged all-to-all, QuACK forward/dgrad GEMMs, Sonic combine, and explicit cuDNN calls for `dw13` and `dw2` ([source](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic_cute.py:111)).

Therefore, `0.026` versus `0.00065` cannot by itself prove that Wgrad caused the difference. Legitimate reduction-order differences in QuACK and combine are confounds.

It remains compelling corroboration because:

- Both paths use identical inputs and the same fp32 dense oracle.
- The no-drop comparison removes capacity-selection differences.
- The cuDNN Wgrad input violates a known contract: every group must be divisible by 256 and the final offset must equal the physical token dimension ([installed facade](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/_bf16_api.py:136)).
- The isolated GB200 reproduction and tiling simulation reproduce the corruption pattern independently.
- The internal kernel itself declares `FIX_PAD_SIZE = 256` ([source](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/wgrad/moe_grouped_gemm_wgrad.py:75)).

One remaining limitation is the gate’s aggregation: `_graddiff` reports the worst statistic across input gradient, `dw13`, and `dw2`, losing which tensor caused it ([source](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py:296)). Per-tensor reporting is needed for localization.

## 2. Is roughly 2.6% consistent at the tiny gate shape?

Yes.

I reconstructed the no-drop routing groups for the four gate seeds. Expert groups contain 17–44 rows. Each call has two experts because four local experts are processed in two chunks.

With legacy eight-row padding and a 64-row K tile, the first expert position in each chunk consumes roughly 16–32 live rows from the second expert, depending on the pair. The second expert reads the large zero tail of its isolated chunk buffer. The contamination is therefore comparable to the first group’s own row count, while the last positional slice remains clean.

The reported 2.3–3.0% is also a compressed metric. `worst_slice_median` divides a slice median absolute error by the sum of two tensor-wide peak magnitudes. It is not a literal 2.6% relative norm or entrywise error. Large corruption in one expert can appear as a few percent under that normalization.

At the prior hero-shaped groups near 100,489 rows, eight-row padding leaves about 48–56 successor rows exposed for representative groups. Under the independent audit’s assumptions of comparable, roughly zero-mean row contributions, the perturbation scale is approximately `sqrt(50 / 100000) ≈ 2.2%`. That is the same order as its 1.7–2.3% prediction. It is a plausibility argument, not a substitute for a hero-shaped GPU comparison.

## 3. Fix recommendation

Use **256-row group alignment**. Do not ship 64.

64 explains the observed internal tile behavior and prevents the measured neighbor reads in cuDNN Frontend 1.27.0, but it remains outside the public contract. The public Torch facade is not a drop-in replacement for this JAX path: it accepts Torch tensors and performs host validation of runtime offsets. A future supported JAX facade would be preferable. Until then, either use `ragged_dot` Wgrad or retain the raw bridge while satisfying and checking the complete 256-row contract.

The coupled changes are:

1. Set the Wgrad group-alignment constant to 256 and verify it equals the installed kernel’s `FIX_PAD_SIZE`.

2. Keep `_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT = 8` and the existing MMA tiles unchanged. Those are different constraints.

3. Fix the ordinary copy path, including the final offset. For physical capacity `C`, alignment `A=256`, and `G` groups, use a static physical size such as:

   ```text
   P = align_up(C, A) + A * (G - 1)
   ```

   Round the first `G-1` group extents to `A`; assign `P - sum(first_extents)` to the final group. Then every extent is divisible by 256 and `offsets[-1] == P == padded.shape[0]`. The added final rows are zero, so assigning them to the last Wgrad group contributes zero.

4. If the prealigned receiver optimization is retained, set `RAGGED_CUDNN_RECEIVER_ALIGNMENT = 256`. Accept only positive multiples of 256. Reject 64 and other values.

5. Give the prealigned receiver the same full-partition property:

   ```text
   receiver_rows = align_up(chunk_capacity, receiver_alignment)
                   + receiver_alignment * (chunk_experts - 1)
   ```

   Transport starts use aligned expert extents. The prealigned Wgrad entry point must add every residual zero row to its final group before taking the cumulative sum. Its last offset must equal `lhs.shape[0]`, not merely the sum of active aligned extents.

6. Keep `ragged_receiver_alignment=None` safe: the transport may remain packed, but the copy wrapper must construct the complete 256-aligned partition. Every accepted explicit alignment must use the prealigned-safe construction.

The concurrent partial change currently visible in [cudnn_wgrad_cute.py](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:97) raises alignment to 256 but still allocates `values.shape[0] + 255 * G` while returning the cumulative rounded active sizes. In general, `padded_offsets[-1] != padded.shape[0]` ([line 115](/home/marin/projects/marin-mfu-loop/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/cudnn_wgrad_cute.py:115)). I would not accept that as contract-complete.

## 4. GPU evidence required before commit

I would require these measurements:

- Run the same ragged transport and identical inputs with only Wgrad changed among `ragged_dot`, legacy alignment 8, alignment 64, and contract-complete alignment 256. Report input gradient, `dw13`, and `dw2` separately, per expert.
- Hold values and group sizes fixed while permuting expert placement. The error should follow the non-final buffer slot, while the final slot remains at the BF16 reference floor.
- Compare the 256 copy path with the 256 prealigned receiver path. They should produce equivalent Wgrads.
- Record every physical group extent and verify `extent % 256 == 0` and `offsets[-1] == operand.shape[0]`.
- Test tiny gate groups, empty groups, highly skewed groups, and hero-shaped dimensions/counts.
- For a representative case, compare the raw JAX bridge with both an fp32 grouped-matmul reference and the public Torch facade. The former checks numerical correctness; the latter checks that the constructed layout is accepted by cuDNN’s supported API.
- Rerun the four-GPU dense-reference gate and one hero-shaped expert-layer backward. Set a tighter `worst_slice_median` threshold only after observing the corrected baseline.
- Measure padding memory and Wgrad latency for both copy and prealigned layouts.

I would keep ragged migration blocked, or temporarily route its weight gradients through `ragged_dot`, until those checks pass.
